item.title: Alexander McClintock Quartet Live — Fri Jul 31, 7:30 PM — The Melon Ball – Watermelon Music
item.description:
The Alexander McClintock Quartet is a group of up-and-coming Sacramento-area musicians: Pianist Colbe Hunter, Bassist Claire Seymour, Drummer JJ Doolittle, and Davis’ own Alexander McClintock on Saxophone. Come join us as we celebrate the jazz giants that have inspired many others, including us, and all the variety of beautiful music that has come out of it. $15 General Admission Show starts at 7:30pm Doors open at 7:00pm This is a BYOB event!
Source: The Dirt

item.title: A Journey into the Hummingbirds' Gardens — Sat Aug 1 — The Paint Chip
item.description:
The Paint Chip Artist of the Month: Lisa Monet Adda. Visit the Paint Chip during August to see “A Journey into the Hummingbirds’ Gardens”, a vibrant collection of photos by nature and bird photographer Lisa Monet Adda. Photographs are available for sale and on display through August 2026 Free Event, all day during business hours
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Davis Farmers Market — Sat Aug 1, 8:00 AM — Central Park
item.description:
Year-round at Central Park in downtown Davis, thousands gather each week to shop for what is grown, raised, and made locally at our markets. We are dedicated to bringing farmers right to your table, so we stay open rain or shine. Walk rows of stalls lined with an array of fruits and vegetables, including certified organic produce, choice meats, chicken, seafood, wine, local eggs and honey. Choose from a variety of fresh-baked goods, plants, flowers and gifts. Enjoy a picnic from one of our many food stands, made from market ingredients. See the vendor list here: https://www.davisfarmersmarket.org/our-sellers/ Farmers Market Hours Central Park: Saturdays 8a–1p (year-round), and Wednesdays 3p–6p (September through March); 4p–8p (April through August) UC Davis – North Quad: Wednesdays 10a–1:30p (fall and spring quarters) Sutter Davis Hospital: Thursdays 10a–1p (May through September) Sutter Medical Center, Sacramento: Thursdays 2:30p–5:30p
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Get to Know Your Sewing Machine! — Sat Aug 1, 10:00 AM — Davis Arts Center
item.description:
Do you have a sewing machine but don’t feel comfortable using it? Now is your chance to become a confident sewing machine user! In this one-day workshop, students will learn basic sewing machine maintenance including how to properly thread their machine, troubleshoot common stitching problems, and gain a better understanding of how their machine works. ● Sewing machines are not provided ● All other materials will be provided ● Children under 8 must be accompanied by an adult Instructor: Courtney Siperstein-Cook ALL AGES Price: $35 Time: 10:00a-1:00p Workshop date: Saturday, August 1
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Discover Berryessa Snow Mountain National Monument with Author Marc Hoshovsky — Sat Aug 1, 11:00 AM — REI Sacramento
item.description:
Learn more about this fascinating landscape, located just west and north of Davis in the northern Coast Ranges. Marc Hoshovsky, coauthor of the recently published guidebook titled, Exploring the Berryessa Snow Mountain National Monument Region, will share the wonders of this landscape, one shaped by ancient tectonic forces, uplifted ocean crust, and volcanic seamounts that have drawn the attention of geologists from around the world. Beyond its scientific significance, the monument offers rugged beauty, diverse wildlife habitats, scenic hiking opportunities, and traces of California’s rich mining heritage waiting to be discovered. Their new guidebook, which will be available for sale and author signing, is well-illustrated, tells captivating stories, and provides detailed maps and route descriptions that allow you to explore the region on your own.
Source: The Dirt

item.description: ROMA DEVANBU SURFACE TENSION July 3 – August 2, 2026 Second Saturday Reception July 11th, 5-8 PM Roma Devanbu has been making and exhibiting her paintings and mix-media work for decades. In Surface Tension, her first exhibit exclusively of photographs, we see her hungry painters eye hunting and gathering brush marks, patterns and textures in the wide world around her. Devanbu says “Inside the studio I manipulate materials. I rub, tear, fold, cut, glue and paint to create images on paper and canvas. item.title: Who are Orientals: Magenta Realism — Sat Aug 1, 12:00 PM — Axis Gallery
item.description: SHARON TSAO WHO ARE ORIENTALS: MAGENTA REALISM July 3 – August 2, 2026 Second Saturday Reception: July 11, 5–8 PM About forty years ago, when I first came to California, I was told that I was “Oriental.” I was also told that certain tables and chests were “Oriental,” and that a particular decorative style was likewise considered “Oriental,” even though these things looked unfamiliar to me. The works in this exhibition are largely produced in what I was told is an “Oriental” style or manner. They originate from dried Boston ivy vines resembling twisted tree branches, gathered after years of growth without human intervention and coated with an artificial magenta surface. The application of magenta coating violently interrupts this natural index. item.title: Misner & Smith Live — Sat Aug 1, 7:30 PM — The Melon Ball – Watermelon Music
item.description: Misner & Smith are a Northern California duo known for their soaring harmonies, finely crafted songwriting, and genre-blending acoustic sound. Formed by Sam Misner and Megan Smith, the pair have spent nearly two decades creating music that draws from folk, Americana, jazz, and rock influences, earning them a reputation for songs that are both poetic and emotionally resonant. Their work is defined by precise, story-driven songwriting paired with an improvisational spirit, a combination that has led critics to describe their music as “beautiful complex poetry.” Their latest album, All Is Song, represents their most transformative work to date—an album shaped by years of writing, reflection, and deep musical exploration. Rooted in their California upbringing—Sam from Sonoma County and Megan from Davis—the duo’s music carries a strong sense of place, often reflecting the landscapes and emotional textures of the region. item.title: Davis Craft and Vintage Fair — Sun Aug 2, 10:00 AM — Central Park – Davis
item.description:
Davis Craft and Vintage Fair began as the Square Tomatoes Craft Fair more than 10 years ago! The event was started by instructors from the UC Davis Craft Center in order to have a monthly craft fair for local artisans and the local community. We embraced local vintage vendors in 2017, we’ve grown and we are still home to local artists and makers from the Davis and greater Sacramento area. We collaborate with local non-profits starting with Couleurs Vives Art Studio who joined us in 2018! Many of our talented vendors can be found at other festivals like the Davis Phoenix Coalition’s Pride Fest, the I-House’s International Festival, and 2nd Friday ArtAbouts on E Street Plaza. Expect to see friendly vendors with local handmade and original art, crafts, quality vintage items, upcycled treasures, earth-friendly creations, good food, and more. Free live music fills the open space for a lively atmosphere so be sure to stop by and join us!
Source: The Dirt

item.title: Art in Action: Marvelous Marionettes — Sun Aug 2, 1:00 PM — Pence Gallery
item.description: Art in Action: Marvelous Marionettes Sunday, August 2, 1-3 PM $5 Members, $10 Non-Members (per person, all materials included) Use your imagination to bring your favorite animal to life! Transform cardboard, various papers, pom poms, yarn, and more into a lively and colorful animal marionette. How it works: Art in Action engages kids in art projects that are fun, creative, and collaborative with their family members. This is a drop-in program for ages 5-12. No registration in advance is required, but space and supplies are limited to the first 25 participants and are available on a first come, first served basis. When you arrive, pay with cash or card at the front desk. A parent or adult caregiver is required to stay, but only has to pay for the project for themselves if they are also doing art. item.title: The Davis Bookworms — Sun Aug 2, 1:30 PM — Nashoba Wines
item.description:
